name: SSC Active Passive Voice
description: Active-passive voice transformations, rules, question forms, modals, imperatives, and traps.

cards.term: Change into passive: The guard checks the bags.
cards.definition:
Passive: The bags are checked by the guard.

Rule: The object becomes the subject, and simple present becomes am/is/are + V3

Example: At station gates, bags are checked so casually that even lunch boxes feel suspicious.

cards.term: Change into passive: She writes a letter.
cards.definition:
Passive: A letter is written by her.

Rule: Simple present passive uses is/am/are + V3

Example: A letter is written by her with handwriting so neat it looks printed.

cards.term: Change into passive: The teacher explains the rule.
cards.definition:
Passive: The rule is explained by the teacher.

Rule: Singular object takes is + V3

Example: The rule is explained by the teacher, then re-explained by the topper at double speed.

cards.term: Change into passive: They clean the classroom.
cards.definition:
Passive: The classroom is cleaned by them.

Rule: Plural/collective object in singular sense takes is if classroom is one place

Example: The classroom is cleaned by them only when inspection becomes a rumour.

cards.term: Change into passive: Farmers grow wheat.
cards.definition:
Passive: Wheat is grown by farmers.

Rule: General object can become passive subject

Example: Wheat is grown by farmers long before it becomes a packet in a kitchen.

cards.term: Change into passive: The police arrest thieves.
cards.definition:
Passive: Thieves are arrested by the police.

Rule: Plural passive subject takes are + V3

Example: Thieves are arrested by the police, not by dramatic background music.

cards.term: Change into passive: People speak Hindi here.
cards.definition:
Passive: Hindi is spoken here.

Rule: When the doer is general, by people is usually omitted

Example: Hindi is spoken here, along with gestures when words fail.

cards.term: Change into passive: We celebrate Diwali.
cards.definition:
Passive: Diwali is celebrated by us.

Rule: Simple present active changes to is celebrated

Example: Diwali is celebrated with lamps, sweets, and impossible cleaning deadlines.

cards.term: Change into passive: The chef cooks dinner.
cards.definition:
Passive: Dinner is cooked by the chef.

Rule: Object dinner becomes subject

Example: Dinner is cooked by the chef, but everyone still gives advice from the sofa.

cards.term: Change into passive: The company sells laptops.
cards.definition:
Passive: Laptops are sold by the company.

Rule: Plural object becomes plural passive subject

Example: Laptops are sold by the company with slogans shinier than the screen.

cards.term: Change into passive: The librarian issues books.
cards.definition:
Passive: Books are issued by the librarian.

Rule: Plural object takes are + V3

Example: Books are issued by the librarian after a stare that says return them on time.

cards.term: Change into passive: The nurse gives medicine.
cards.definition:
Passive: Medicine is given by the nurse.

Rule: Uncountable object takes singular verb

Example: Medicine is given by the nurse with more punctuality than most alarms.

cards.term: Change into passive: The postman delivers letters.
cards.definition:
Passive: Letters are delivered by the postman.

Rule: Plural object takes are + V3

Example: Letters are delivered by the postman, carrying news slower but warmer than notifications.

cards.term: Change into passive: My mother makes tea.
cards.definition:
Passive: Tea is made by my mother.

Rule: Uncountable object tea takes is

Example: Tea is made by my mother, and peace returns to the house for seven minutes.

cards.term: Change into passive: The mechanic repairs bikes.
cards.definition:
Passive: Bikes are repaired by the mechanic.

Rule: Plural object becomes passive subject

Example: Bikes are repaired by the mechanic after he listens to the engine like a doctor.

cards.term: Change into passive: The gardener waters the plants.
cards.definition:
Passive: The plants are watered by the gardener.

Rule: Plural object takes are + V3

Example: The plants are watered by the gardener, while the weeds grow without invitation.

cards.term: Change into passive: Students solve the puzzle.
cards.definition:
Passive: The puzzle is solved by students.

Rule: Singular object takes is + V3

Example: The puzzle is solved by students after blaming the question for ten minutes.

cards.term: Change into passive: The shopkeeper weighs the rice.
cards.definition:
Passive: The rice is weighed by the shopkeeper.

Rule: Uncountable noun rice takes is

Example: The rice is weighed by the shopkeeper with a scale older than the shop.

cards.term: Change into passive: Children fly kites.
cards.definition:
Passive: Kites are flown by children.

Rule: Fly becomes flown in passive

Example: Kites are flown by children, and every terrace becomes an airport.

cards.term: Change into passive: The artist paints portraits.
cards.definition:
Passive: Portraits are painted by the artist.

Rule: Plural object takes are painted

Example: Portraits are painted by the artist, who makes even serious faces look poetic.

cards.term: Change into passive: The hunter shot the arrow.
cards.definition:
Passive: The arrow was shot by the hunter.

Rule: Simple past passive uses was/were + V3

Example: The arrow was shot by the hunter, but the target had already chosen drama.

cards.term: Change into passive: She solved the problem.
cards.definition:
Passive: The problem was solved by her.

Rule: Past tense changes to was/were + V3

Example: The problem was solved by her before the calculator could feel important.

cards.term: Change into passive: They built the bridge.
cards.definition:
Passive: The bridge was built by them.

Rule: Singular object takes was

Example: The bridge was built by them, saving villagers from the daily boat adventure.

cards.term: Change into passive: The storm damaged the roof.
cards.definition:
Passive: The roof was damaged by the storm.

Rule: Object roof becomes subject

Example: The roof was damaged by the storm, and the bucket became emergency technology.

cards.term: Change into passive: The committee approved the plan.
cards.definition:
Passive: The plan was approved by the committee.

Rule: Simple past passive uses was approved

Example: The plan was approved by the committee after only four rounds of tea.

cards.term: Change into passive: The king defeated the enemy.
cards.definition:
Passive: The enemy was defeated by the king.

Rule: Past V2 changes to was + V3

Example: The enemy was defeated by the king, at least according to the royal poet.

cards.term: Change into passive: The child broke the cup.
cards.definition:
Passive: The cup was broken by the child.

Rule: Break becomes broken

Example: The cup was broken by the child, while gravity was blamed as co-accused.

cards.term: Change into passive: The driver stopped the bus.
cards.definition:
Passive: The bus was stopped by the driver.

Rule: Simple past active becomes was stopped

Example: The bus was stopped by the driver exactly one metre after the stop.

cards.term: Change into passive: The editor corrected the article.
cards.definition:
Passive: The article was corrected by the editor.

Rule: Object becomes passive subject

Example: The article was corrected by the editor, and half the adjectives disappeared.

cards.term: Change into passive: The police caught the thief.
cards.definition:
Passive: The thief was caught by the police.

Rule: Catch becomes caught

Example: The thief was caught by the police because running in slippers is poor planning.

cards.term: Change into passive: The carpenter made a chair.
cards.definition:
Passive: A chair was made by the carpenter.

Rule: Make becomes made

Example: A chair was made by the carpenter, and everyone tested it like a government bridge.

cards.term: Change into passive: The doctor examined the patient.
cards.definition:
Passive: The patient was examined by the doctor.

Rule: Simple past passive uses was examined

Example: The patient was examined by the doctor, not by the waiting-room rumours.

cards.term: Change into passive: The teacher praised the student.
cards.definition:
Passive: The student was praised by the teacher.

Rule: Object student becomes subject

Example: The student was praised by the teacher, creating instant jealousy in row two.

cards.term: Change into passive: The dog chased the cat.
cards.definition:
Passive: The cat was chased by the dog.

Rule: Past passive uses was chased

Example: The cat was chased by the dog, but escaped with royal dignity.

cards.term: Change into passive: The manager signed the document.
cards.definition:
Passive: The document was signed by the manager.

Rule: Object document becomes subject

Example: The document was signed by the manager after the pen was searched like treasure.

cards.term: Change into passive: The soldiers guarded the fort.
cards.definition:
Passive: The fort was guarded by the soldiers.

Rule: Simple past passive uses was + V3

Example: The fort was guarded by the soldiers through a night colder than discipline.

cards.term: Change into passive: The villagers repaired the road.
cards.definition:
Passive: The road was repaired by the villagers.

Rule: Past passive with singular object uses was

Example: The road was repaired by the villagers, proving meetings are not the only solution.

cards.term: Change into passive: The tailor stitched the shirt.
cards.definition:
Passive: The shirt was stitched by the tailor.

Rule: Stitch becomes stitched

Example: The shirt was stitched by the tailor with more precision than a geometry diagram.

cards.term: Change into passive: The captain won the match.
cards.definition:
Passive: The match was won by the captain.

Rule: Win becomes won

Example: The match was won by the captain, and the speech was won by the sponsor.

cards.term: Change into passive: The students decorated the hall.
cards.definition:
Passive: The hall was decorated by the students.

Rule: Simple past passive uses was decorated

Example: The hall was decorated by the students until even the fan looked festive.

cards.term: Change into passive: She is reading a novel.
cards.definition:
Passive: A novel is being read by her.

Rule: Present continuous passive uses is/am/are being + V3

Example: A novel is being read by her while the bookmark waits for respect.

cards.term: Change into passive: They are painting the wall.
cards.definition:
Passive: The wall is being painted by them.

Rule: Object wall is singular, so use is being + V3

Example: The wall is being painted by them, and the floor is also receiving free decoration.

cards.term: Change into passive: The chef is preparing soup.
cards.definition:
Passive: Soup is being prepared by the chef.

Rule: Present continuous active changes to is being prepared

Example: Soup is being prepared by the chef, and everyone is pretending patience.

cards.term: Change into passive: The mechanic is repairing the scooter.
cards.definition:
Passive: The scooter is being repaired by the mechanic.

Rule: Use being before V3 in continuous passive

Example: The scooter is being repaired by the mechanic after making sounds like a wounded robot.

cards.term: Change into passive: The teacher is checking notebooks.
cards.definition:
Passive: Notebooks are being checked by the teacher.

Rule: Plural object takes are being + V3

Example: Notebooks are being checked by the teacher, and red ink is working overtime.

cards.term: Change into passive: The workers are laying the pipes.
cards.definition:
Passive: The pipes are being laid by the workers.

Rule: Lay becomes laid

Example: The pipes are being laid by the workers under a road that was repaired last week.

cards.term: Change into passive: The boys are flying kites.
cards.definition:
Passive: Kites are being flown by the boys.

Rule: Present continuous passive uses are being flown

Example: Kites are being flown by the boys while parents shout weather advice.

cards.term: Change into passive: The gardener is cutting the grass.
cards.definition:
Passive: The grass is being cut by the gardener.

Rule: Uncountable/singular grass takes is being

Example: The grass is being cut by the gardener, and the lawn looks suddenly disciplined.

cards.term: Change into passive: The police are questioning the suspect.
cards.definition:
Passive: The suspect is being questioned by the police.

Rule: Object suspect is singular

Example: The suspect is being questioned by the police, and silence is becoming suspicious.

cards.term: Change into passive: The engineers are testing the machine.
cards.definition:
Passive: The machine is being tested by the engineers.

Rule: Present continuous passive pattern is being + V3

Example: The machine is being tested by the engineers like it is giving an exam.

cards.term: Change into passive: He is writing an email.
cards.definition:
Passive: An email is being written by him.

Rule: Object email becomes subject

Example: An email is being written by him, with more drafts than decisions.

cards.term: Change into passive: They are building a flyover.
cards.definition:
Passive: A flyover is being built by them.

Rule: Build becomes built

Example: A flyover is being built by them, turning traffic into a patience course.

cards.term: Change into passive: The nurse is giving an injection.
cards.definition:
Passive: An injection is being given by the nurse.

Rule: Give becomes given

Example: An injection is being given by the nurse while the patient studies the ceiling.

cards.term: Change into passive: My brother is cleaning the fan.
cards.definition:
Passive: The fan is being cleaned by my brother.

Rule: Present continuous passive uses is being cleaned

Example: The fan is being cleaned by my brother, and ancient dust is losing territory.

cards.term: Change into passive: The host is serving dinner.
cards.definition:
Passive: Dinner is being served by the host.

Rule: Dinner as object becomes passive subject

Example: Dinner is being served by the host, and manners have entered the room.

cards.term: Change into passive: She was writing a poem.
cards.definition:
Passive: A poem was being written by her.

Rule: Past continuous passive uses was/were being + V3

Example: A poem was being written by her while rain did half the background work.

cards.term: Change into passive: They were repairing the bridge.
cards.definition:
Passive: The bridge was being repaired by them.

Rule: Singular object takes was being + V3

Example: The bridge was being repaired by them, and commuters invented new complaints.

cards.term: Change into passive: The children were flying kites.
cards.definition:
Passive: Kites were being flown by the children.

Rule: Plural passive subject takes were being

Example: Kites were being flown by the children before the storm joined the game.

cards.term: Change into passive: The police were chasing the thief.
cards.definition:
Passive: The thief was being chased by the police.

Rule: Past continuous passive uses was being chased

Example: The thief was being chased by the police and betrayed by his slippers.

cards.term: Change into passive: The chef was baking a cake.
cards.definition:
Passive: A cake was being baked by the chef.

Rule: Object cake becomes passive subject

Example: A cake was being baked by the chef, and the smell was already public property.

cards.term: Change into passive: The students were cleaning the hall.
cards.definition:
Passive: The hall was being cleaned by the students.

Rule: Singular object takes was being

Example: The hall was being cleaned by the students for inspection day.

cards.term: Change into passive: The workers were digging the well.
cards.definition:
Passive: The well was being dug by the workers.

Rule: Dig becomes dug

Example: The well was being dug by the workers, one basket of earth at a time.

cards.term: Change into passive: The tailor was stitching the uniform.
cards.definition:
Passive: The uniform was being stitched by the tailor.

Rule: Past continuous passive uses was being + V3

Example: The uniform was being stitched by the tailor just before school reopened.

cards.term: Change into passive: The mechanic was fixing the engine.
cards.definition:
Passive: The engine was being fixed by the mechanic.

Rule: Object engine becomes subject

Example: The engine was being fixed by the mechanic while everyone gave expert advice.

cards.term: Change into passive: The artist was sketching a portrait.
cards.definition:
Passive: A portrait was being sketched by the artist.

Rule: Past continuous passive pattern

Example: A portrait was being sketched by the artist, and the model was losing patience.

cards.term: Change into passive: She has completed the work.
cards.definition:
Passive: The work has been completed by her.

Rule: Present perfect passive uses has/have been + V3

Example: The work has been completed by her before panic could become official.

cards.term: Change into passive: They have solved the puzzle.
cards.definition:
Passive: The puzzle has been solved by them.

Rule: Singular object takes has been

Example: The puzzle has been solved by them after blaming the puzzle for being rude.

cards.term: Change into passive: The police have arrested the thief.
cards.definition:
Passive: The thief has been arrested by the police.

Rule: Present perfect passive uses has been arrested

Example: The thief has been arrested by the police, ending his short motivational speech.

cards.term: Change into passive: The committee has approved the proposal.
cards.definition:
Passive: The proposal has been approved by the committee.

Rule: Object proposal is singular, so has been + V3

Example: The proposal has been approved by the committee after surviving three subcommittees.

cards.term: Change into passive: The students have submitted the forms.
cards.definition:
Passive: The forms have been submitted by the students.

Rule: Plural object takes have been

Example: The forms have been submitted by the students, mostly at the last possible minute.

cards.term: Change into passive: The gardener has watered the plants.
cards.definition:
Passive: The plants have been watered by the gardener.

Rule: Plural subject plants takes have been

Example: The plants have been watered by the gardener, while the cactus judges everyone.

cards.term: Change into passive: The doctor has examined the patient.
cards.definition:
Passive: The patient has been examined by the doctor.

Rule: Present perfect passive pattern

Example: The patient has been examined by the doctor, and the prescription has begun its mystery life.

cards.term: Change into passive: The company has launched a product.
cards.definition:
Passive: A product has been launched by the company.

Rule: Object product becomes subject

Example: A product has been launched by the company with a name nobody can pronounce.

cards.term: Change into passive: The teacher has corrected the papers.
cards.definition:
Passive: The papers have been corrected by the teacher.

Rule: Plural object takes have been corrected

Example: The papers have been corrected by the teacher, and red circles are everywhere.

cards.term: Change into passive: They have postponed the meeting.
cards.definition:
Passive: The meeting has been postponed by them.

Rule: Postpone becomes postponed

Example: The meeting has been postponed, proving that calendars also suffer.

cards.term: Change into passive: She had finished the report.
cards.definition:
Passive: The report had been finished by her.

Rule: Past perfect passive uses had been + V3

Example: The report had been finished by her before the boss invented new changes.

cards.term: Change into passive: They had built the house.
cards.definition:
Passive: The house had been built by them.

Rule: Object house becomes passive subject

Example: The house had been built by them before the road reached it.

cards.term: Change into passive: The police had caught the criminals.
cards.definition:
Passive: The criminals had been caught by the police.

Rule: Past perfect passive uses had been caught

Example: The criminals had been caught by the police before the news channels warmed up.

cards.term: Change into passive: The students had cleaned the classroom.
cards.definition:
Passive: The classroom had been cleaned by the students.

Rule: Had been + V3 is used in past perfect passive

Example: The classroom had been cleaned by the students, shocking the dust population.

cards.term: Change into passive: The mechanic had repaired the car.
cards.definition:
Passive: The car had been repaired by the mechanic.

Rule: Object car becomes passive subject

Example: The car had been repaired by the mechanic before the owner asked ten more questions.

cards.term: Change into passive: The farmer had harvested the crop.
cards.definition:
Passive: The crop had been harvested by the farmer.

Rule: Past perfect passive pattern

Example: The crop had been harvested by the farmer before the rain arrived.

cards.term: Change into passive: They had cancelled the match.
cards.definition:
Passive: The match had been cancelled by them.

Rule: Cancel becomes cancelled

Example: The match had been cancelled, and the spectators became philosophers.

cards.term: Change into passive: The clerk had typed the letter.
cards.definition:
Passive: The letter had been typed by the clerk.

Rule: Had + V3 changes to had been + V3

Example: The letter had been typed by the clerk on a keyboard older than the office.

cards.term: Change into passive: The army had captured the fort.
cards.definition:
Passive: The fort had been captured by the army.

Rule: Past perfect passive uses had been captured

Example: The fort had been captured by the army before sunrise.

cards.term: Change into passive: She had packed the bags.
cards.definition:
Passive: The bags had been packed by her.

Rule: Plural object becomes passive subject but had remains same

Example: The bags had been packed by her, but the charger still escaped.

cards.term: Change into passive: She will write the letter.
cards.definition:
Passive: The letter will be written by her.

Rule: Simple future passive uses will be + V3

Example: The letter will be written by her, probably after three mental drafts.

cards.term: Change into passive: They will finish the project.
cards.definition:
Passive: The project will be finished by them.

Rule: Will + V1 becomes will be + V3

Example: The project will be finished by them, according to the most hopeful slide.

cards.term: Change into passive: The doctor will examine the patient.
cards.definition:
Passive: The patient will be examined by the doctor.

Rule: Object becomes subject after will be + V3

Example: The patient will be examined by the doctor before the relatives diagnose everything.

cards.term: Change into passive: The company will announce the result.
cards.definition:
Passive: The result will be announced by the company.

Rule: Future passive pattern

Example: The result will be announced by the company, and refresh buttons will suffer.

cards.term: Change into passive: We shall help the poor.
cards.definition:
Passive: The poor shall be helped by us.

Rule: Shall passive uses shall be + V3

Example: The poor shall be helped by us, not just mentioned in speeches.

cards.term: Change into passive: He can solve this problem.
cards.definition:
Passive: This problem can be solved by him.

Rule: Modal passive uses modal + be + V3

Example: This problem can be solved by him if the phone stops vibrating.

cards.term: Change into passive: She can speak English.
cards.definition:
Passive: English can be spoken by her.

Rule: Can changes to can be + V3

Example: English can be spoken by her, especially when confidence enters first.

cards.term: Change into passive: They may cancel the trip.
cards.definition:
Passive: The trip may be cancelled by them.

Rule: May passive uses may be + V3

Example: The trip may be cancelled by them, which is how group plans usually evolve.

cards.term: Change into passive: The teacher may punish him.
cards.definition:
Passive: He may be punished by the teacher.

Rule: Object him becomes he in passive

Example: He may be punished by the teacher if the chalk evidence matches.

cards.term: Change into passive: You must obey the rules.
cards.definition:
Passive: The rules must be obeyed by you.

Rule: Must passive uses must be + V3

Example: The rules must be obeyed, even by the person who thinks they are optional.

cards.term: Change into passive: We must finish the task.
cards.definition:
Passive: The task must be finished by us.

Rule: Must + V1 becomes must be + V3

Example: The task must be finished by us before the deadline becomes a horror story.

cards.term: Change into passive: They should respect elders.
cards.definition:
Passive: Elders should be respected by them.

Rule: Should passive uses should be + V3

Example: Elders should be respected, even when their advice arrives in bulk.

cards.term: Change into passive: You should write the answer neatly.
cards.definition:
Passive: The answer should be written neatly by you.

Rule: Should be + V3 forms modal passive

Example: The answer should be written neatly because examiners are human too.

cards.term: Change into passive: The government ought to support farmers.
cards.definition:
Passive: Farmers ought to be supported by the government.

Rule: Ought to passive uses ought to be + V3

Example: Farmers ought to be supported, not remembered only during speeches.

cards.term: Change into passive: We have to complete the form.
cards.definition:
Passive: The form has to be completed by us.

Rule: Have to passive changes according to passive subject

Example: The form has to be completed before the website decides to sleep.

cards.term: Change into passive: She has to submit the file.
cards.definition:
Passive: The file has to be submitted by her.

Rule: Has to passive uses has to be + V3

Example: The file has to be submitted by her before the clerk asks for another copy.

cards.term: Change into passive: They had to repair the road.
cards.definition:
Passive: The road had to be repaired by them.

Rule: Had to passive uses had to be + V3

Example: The road had to be repaired after the potholes became landmarks.

cards.term: Change into passive: He is going to sell the bike.
cards.definition:
Passive: The bike is going to be sold by him.

Rule: Going to passive uses going to be + V3

Example: The bike is going to be sold by him, though his memories are still bargaining.

cards.term: Change into passive: They are going to open a shop.
cards.definition:
Passive: A shop is going to be opened by them.

Rule: Object shop becomes passive subject

Example: A shop is going to be opened by them, and relatives have already suggested names.

cards.term: Change into passive: No one can deny the truth.
cards.definition:
Passive: The truth cannot be denied.

Rule: When doer is general, omit by no one and use cannot be denied

Example: The truth cannot be denied, although it can be delayed with excuses.

cards.term: Change into passive: Open the door.
cards.definition:
Passive: Let the door be opened.

Rule: Imperative passive often begins with let + object + be + V3

Example: Let the door be opened before everyone starts knocking like a drumline.

cards.term: Change into passive: Close the window.
cards.definition:
Passive: Let the window be closed.

Rule: Command passive uses let + object + be + V3

Example: Let the window be closed before mosquitoes file an entry request.

cards.term: Change into passive: Complete the work.
cards.definition:
Passive: Let the work be completed.

Rule: Imperative passive uses let construction

Example: Let the work be completed before motivation expires.

cards.term: Change into passive: Do not waste water.
cards.definition:
Passive: Let water not be wasted.

Rule: Negative imperative passive uses let + object + not be + V3

Example: Let water not be wasted because every dripping tap writes a bill.

cards.term: Change into passive: Do not pluck flowers.
cards.definition:
Passive: Let flowers not be plucked.

Rule: Negative command changes to let + object + not be + V3

Example: Let flowers not be plucked just to die in a selfie.

cards.term: Change into passive: Respect your elders.
cards.definition:
Passive: Let your elders be respected.

Rule: Imperative passive can be made with let

Example: Let your elders be respected, even when their stories have sequels.

cards.term: Change into passive: Help the poor.
cards.definition:
Passive: Let the poor be helped.

Rule: Imperative passive uses let + object + be + V3

Example: Let the poor be helped with action, not just captions.

cards.term: Change into passive: Keep the room clean.
cards.definition:
Passive: Let the room be kept clean.

Rule: Keep becomes be kept in passive

Example: Let the room be kept clean before guests reveal the truth.

cards.term: Change into passive: Switch off the fan.
cards.definition:
Passive: Let the fan be switched off.

Rule: Phrasal verb stays together in passive

Example: Let the fan be switched off when nobody is in the room.

cards.term: Change into passive: Call the doctor.
cards.definition:
Passive: Let the doctor be called.

Rule: Command passive uses let + object + be called

Example: Let the doctor be called before home remedies start competing.

cards.term: Change into passive: Post the letter.
cards.definition:
Passive: Let the letter be posted.

Rule: Object letter becomes passive subject

Example: Let the letter be posted, not kept forever in the drawer.

cards.term: Change into passive: Solve this question.
cards.definition:
Passive: Let this question be solved.

Rule: Imperative passive with this question as object

Example: Let this question be solved before it becomes personal.

cards.term: Change into passive: Read the instructions carefully.
cards.definition:
Passive: Let the instructions be read carefully.

Rule: Adverb remains with passive sentence

Example: Let the instructions be read carefully, a rare but powerful exam strategy.

cards.term: Change into passive: Do not disturb the patient.
cards.definition:
Passive: Let the patient not be disturbed.

Rule: Negative imperative passive pattern

Example: Let the patient not be disturbed, especially by relatives with medical theories.

cards.term: Change into passive: Never insult the weak.
cards.definition:
Passive: Let the weak never be insulted.

Rule: Never stays before passive be phrase

Example: Let the weak never be insulted, because strength without kindness is cheap.

cards.term: Change into passive: Does she write poems?
cards.definition:
Passive: Are poems written by her?

Rule: Simple present question passive uses am/is/are + subject + V3

Example: Are poems written by her, or do they simply appear during rain?

cards.term: Change into passive: Do they sell books?
cards.definition:
Passive: Are books sold by them?

Rule: Do/does questions become is/are + object + V3

Example: Are books sold by them, or only recommended dramatically?

cards.term: Change into passive: Did he break the window?
cards.definition:
Passive: Was the window broken by him?

Rule: Did + V1 changes to was/were + V3

Example: Was the window broken by him, or did the cricket ball act alone?

cards.term: Change into passive: Did the police catch the thief?
cards.definition:
Passive: Was the thief caught by the police?

Rule: Past question passive uses was/were + subject + V3

Example: Was the thief caught by the police before he changed slippers?

cards.term: Change into passive: Is she reading a book?
cards.definition:
Passive: Is a book being read by her?

Rule: Present continuous question passive uses is/are + object + being + V3

Example: Is a book being read by her, or is it just protecting the phone screen?

cards.term: Change into passive: Are they painting the wall?
cards.definition:
Passive: Is the wall being painted by them?

Rule: Continuous passive uses being + V3

Example: Is the wall being painted by them, or is the floor receiving most of it?

cards.term: Change into passive: Was he writing a letter?
cards.definition:
Passive: Was a letter being written by him?

Rule: Past continuous question passive uses was/were being + V3

Example: Was a letter being written by him before the ink betrayed him?

cards.term: Change into passive: Were they repairing the road?
cards.definition:
Passive: Was the road being repaired by them?

Rule: Object road is singular, so was being repaired

Example: Was the road being repaired by them, or merely surrounded by cones?

cards.term: Change into passive: Has she completed the task?
cards.definition:
Passive: Has the task been completed by her?

Rule: Present perfect question passive uses has/have + object + been + V3

Example: Has the task been completed by her, or is it in the sacred folder called pending?

cards.term: Change into passive: Have they submitted the forms?
cards.definition:
Passive: Have the forms been submitted by them?

Rule: Plural passive subject takes have been

Example: Have the forms been submitted by them before the server grows moody?

cards.term: Change into passive: Had he signed the document?
cards.definition:
Passive: Had the document been signed by him?

Rule: Past perfect question passive uses had + object + been + V3

Example: Had the document been signed by him before the pen vanished?

cards.term: Change into passive: Will she finish the work?
cards.definition:
Passive: Will the work be finished by her?

Rule: Future question passive uses will + object + be + V3

Example: Will the work be finished by her before the reminder turns red?

cards.term: Change into passive: Can he solve the puzzle?
cards.definition:
Passive: Can the puzzle be solved by him?

Rule: Modal question passive uses modal + object + be + V3

Example: Can the puzzle be solved by him, or will option C receive blind faith?

cards.term: Change into passive: Should we follow the rules?
cards.definition:
Passive: Should the rules be followed by us?

Rule: Should question passive uses should + object + be + V3

Example: Should the rules be followed by us even when nobody is looking? Yes, especially then.

cards.term: Change into passive: Who wrote this letter?
cards.definition:
Passive: By whom was this letter written?

Rule: When who is the subject in active, passive often begins with by whom

Example: By whom was this letter written? The handwriting has become a crime scene.

cards.term: Change into passive: Who broke the glass?
cards.definition:
Passive: By whom was the glass broken?

Rule: Who as doer becomes by whom in passive

Example: By whom was the glass broken, and why is the child suddenly silent?

cards.term: Change into passive: Whom did you invite?
cards.definition:
Passive: Who was invited by you?

Rule: Whom as object becomes subject who in passive

Example: Who was invited by you, and did snacks know about it?

cards.term: Change into passive: What did he buy?
cards.definition:
Passive: What was bought by him?

Rule: Question word object remains at the beginning in passive

Example: What was bought by him that required such a large bag?

cards.term: Change into passive: Which book did she choose?
cards.definition:
Passive: Which book was chosen by her?

Rule: Object phrase becomes passive subject

Example: Which book was chosen by her, the easy one or the one pretending to be easy?

cards.term: Change into passive: Why did they cancel the match?
cards.definition:
Passive: Why was the match cancelled by them?

Rule: Keep why at the beginning and form past passive question

Example: Why was the match cancelled by them, and why did they tell us after we arrived?

cards.term: Change into passive: She gave me a pen.
cards.definition:
Passive: I was given a pen by her.

Rule: With two objects, the indirect object can become passive subject

Example: I was given a pen by her, which disappeared before the next period.

cards.term: Change into passive: He taught us English.
cards.definition:
Passive: We were taught English by him.

Rule: Indirect object us becomes subject we

Example: We were taught English by him, including the art of fearing articles.

cards.term: Change into passive: They offered him a job.
cards.definition:
Passive: He was offered a job by them.

Rule: Indirect object him becomes passive subject he

Example: He was offered a job by them, and suddenly everyone gave career advice.

cards.term: Change into passive: She told me a story.
cards.definition:
Passive: I was told a story by her.

Rule: Indirect object me becomes subject I

Example: I was told a story by her that began normally and ended with a ghost.

cards.term: Change into passive: The teacher asked him a question.
cards.definition:
Passive: He was asked a question by the teacher.

Rule: Indirect object him becomes he

Example: He was asked a question by the teacher, and his confidence left early.

cards.term: Change into passive: The company sent her an email.
cards.definition:
Passive: She was sent an email by the company.

Rule: Indirect object her becomes she

Example: She was sent an email by the company, which began with unfortunately.

cards.term: Change into passive: My uncle bought me a watch.
cards.definition:
Passive: I was bought a watch by my uncle.

Rule: Indirect object me becomes I

Example: I was bought a watch by my uncle, and now I am officially expected to be punctual.

cards.term: Change into passive: She made him tea.
cards.definition:
Passive: He was made tea by her.

Rule: Indirect object him becomes he

Example: He was made tea by her, which is the purest form of apology.

cards.term: Change into active: The letter was written by Sita.
cards.definition:
Active: Sita wrote the letter.

Rule: To change passive to active, make the by-object the subject and restore the active verb

Example: Sita wrote the letter, and the paper somehow looked more confident.

cards.term: Change into active: The match was won by India.
cards.definition:
Active: India won the match.

Rule: Passive was/were + V3 changes to simple past active

Example: India won the match, and the colony discovered fireworks.

cards.term: Change into active: The thief has been caught by the police.
cards.definition:
Active: The police have caught the thief.

Rule: Has been + V3 changes to has/have + V3 according to active subject

Example: The police have caught the thief, whose running shoes failed democracy.

cards.term: Change into active: The work will be finished by them.
cards.definition:
Active: They will finish the work.

Rule: Will be + V3 changes to will + V1

Example: They will finish the work, possibly after inventing one final delay.

cards.term: Change into active: The room is being cleaned by the boys.
cards.definition:
Active: The boys are cleaning the room.

Rule: Is being + V3 changes to is/am/are + V-ing

Example: The boys are cleaning the room because guests are more powerful than rules.

cards.term: Change into active: The road was being repaired by the workers.
cards.definition:
Active: The workers were repairing the road.

Rule: Was being + V3 changes to was/were + V-ing

Example: The workers were repairing the road while traffic practised patience.

cards.term: Change into active: The proposal has been approved by the committee.
cards.definition:
Active: The committee has approved the proposal.

Rule: Has been approved changes to has approved

Example: The committee has approved the proposal after turning it into paperwork sculpture.

cards.term: Change into active: The song is sung by her.
cards.definition:
Active: She sings the song.

Rule: Simple present passive becomes simple present active

Example: She sings the song like the microphone personally encouraged her.

cards.term: Change into active: The ball was thrown by the child.
cards.definition:
Active: The child threw the ball.

Rule: Was + V3 changes to past tense active

Example: The child threw the ball, and the window immediately became nervous.

cards.term: Change into active: The rules must be obeyed by everyone.
cards.definition:
Active: Everyone must obey the rules.

Rule: Modal passive becomes modal + base verb

Example: Everyone must obey the rules, including the rule-maker's favourite nephew.

cards.term: Change into active: The answer should be written clearly by you.
cards.definition:
Active: You should write the answer clearly.

Rule: Should be + V3 becomes should + V1

Example: You should write the answer clearly because examiners do not read minds.

cards.term: Change into active: The medicine was given by the nurse.
cards.definition:
Active: The nurse gave the medicine.

Rule: Past passive becomes simple past active

Example: The nurse gave the medicine with military-level timing.

cards.term: Change into active: The plants have been watered by the gardener.
cards.definition:
Active: The gardener has watered the plants.

Rule: Have been + V3 changes to has/have + V3

Example: The gardener has watered the plants, while the weeds celebrated too.

cards.term: Change into active: The machine is tested by engineers.
cards.definition:
Active: Engineers test the machine.

Rule: Simple present passive becomes simple present active

Example: Engineers test the machine before customers test their patience.

cards.term: Change into active: The bridge had been built by them.
cards.definition:
Active: They had built the bridge.

Rule: Had been + V3 becomes had + V3

Example: They had built the bridge before the first selfie was taken.

cards.term: Can this be changed into passive? He sleeps early.
cards.definition:
Answer: No normal passive form.

Rule: Intransitive verbs like sleep have no object, so passive voice is not possible

Example: He sleeps early, but sleep cannot be slept by him in standard grammar.

cards.term: Can this be changed into passive? The baby cried loudly.
cards.definition:
Answer: No normal passive form.

Rule: Cry is intransitive here and has no object

Example: The baby cried loudly, and the whole house accepted defeat.

cards.term: Can this be changed into passive? She arrived late.
cards.definition:
Answer: No normal passive form.

Rule: Arrive is intransitive and cannot be passivised

Example: She arrived late, and the excuse arrived later.

cards.term: Can this be changed into passive? He died in 2010.
cards.definition:
Answer: No normal passive form.

Rule: Die is intransitive and is not used in passive voice

Example: He died in 2010, but his work may still live.

cards.term: Can this be changed into passive? The accident happened yesterday.
cards.definition:
Answer: No normal passive form.

Rule: Happen is intransitive, so do not write was happened

Example: The accident happened yesterday, not was happened.

cards.term: Can this be changed into passive? The sun rises in the east.
cards.definition:
Answer: No normal passive form.

Rule: Rise is intransitive and has no object

Example: The sun rises in the east without needing a by-phrase.

cards.term: Can this be changed into passive? The meeting took place at noon.
cards.definition:
Answer: No normal passive form.

Rule: Take place is intransitive as a phrase

Example: The meeting took place at noon and ended at an unknown century.

cards.term: Can this be changed into passive? The child fell down.
cards.definition:
Answer: No normal passive form.

Rule: Fall is intransitive here

Example: The child fell down, then checked if anyone was watching.

cards.term: Can this be changed into passive? The price increased suddenly.
cards.definition:
Answer: No normal passive form in this sentence.

Rule: Increase is intransitive here because no doer acts on an object

Example: The price increased suddenly, and wallets held an emergency meeting.

cards.term: Can this be changed into passive? She resembles her mother.
cards.definition:
Answer: Passive is not normally used.

Rule: Some stative/transitive verbs like resemble are not normally passivised in exam grammar

Example: She resembles her mother so much that old neighbours need a second look.

cards.term: Can this be changed into passive? This box contains books.
cards.definition:
Answer: Passive is possible but uncommon: Books are contained in this box.

Rule: Some stative verbs form awkward passives, so use cautiously

Example: This box contains books, dust, and one ancient bookmark.

cards.term: Can this be changed into passive? He has a car.
cards.definition:
Answer: Passive is not normally used.

Rule: Have meaning possession is not normally changed into passive

Example: He has a car, but grammar does not say a car is had by him.

cards.term: Can this be changed into passive? The shirt fits me.
cards.definition:
Answer: Passive is not normally used.

Rule: Fit in this sense is stative and not normally passive

Example: The shirt fits me, which is rare enough to celebrate.

cards.term: Can this be changed into passive? The exam lasted three hours.
cards.definition:
Answer: No passive form.

Rule: Last meaning continue for a duration is intransitive

Example: The exam lasted three hours and aged everyone by three months.

cards.term: Can this be changed into passive? The road leads to the temple.
cards.definition:
Answer: No normal passive form.

Rule: Lead to as in direction is intransitive-like and not usually passive

Example: The road leads to the temple, but the shortcut leads to confusion.

cards.term: Change into passive: I helped him.
cards.definition:
Passive: He was helped by me.

Rule: Object pronoun him becomes subject pronoun he in passive

Example: He was helped by me after his confidence ran out of battery.

cards.term: Change into passive: He praised me.
cards.definition:
Passive: I was praised by him.

Rule: Object me becomes subject I

Example: I was praised by him, and my notebook suddenly looked proud.

cards.term: Change into passive: They invited us.
cards.definition:
Passive: We were invited by them.

Rule: Object us becomes subject we

Example: We were invited by them after the snacks were confirmed.

cards.term: Change into passive: We supported them.
cards.definition:
Passive: They were supported by us.

Rule: Object them becomes subject they

Example: They were supported by us when the plan almost collapsed.

cards.term: Change into passive: She scolded him.
cards.definition:
Passive: He was scolded by her.

Rule: Object him changes to he

Example: He was scolded by her, and the room became educational.

cards.term: Change into passive: He trusted her.
cards.definition:
Passive: She was trusted by him.

Rule: Object her changes to she

Example: She was trusted by him with the password, which was brave.

cards.term: Change into passive: They ignored me.
cards.definition:
Passive: I was ignored by them.

Rule: Object me becomes subject I

Example: I was ignored by them with professional-level silence.

cards.term: Change into passive: I respect you.
cards.definition:
Passive: You are respected by me.

Rule: You stays you in subject/object form

Example: You are respected by me, especially when you return borrowed pens.

cards.term: Change into passive: He blamed us.
cards.definition:
Passive: We were blamed by him.

Rule: Object us becomes subject we

Example: We were blamed by him because responsibility needed a landing place.

cards.term: Change into passive: She warned them.
cards.definition:
Passive: They were warned by her.

Rule: Object them becomes subject they

Example: They were warned by her, but confidence wore earplugs.
